paper.abstract: Abstract Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) equips large language models (LLMs) with tool-use capabilities that substantially improve reasoning on complex tasks. However, integrating external tools often destabilizes training: over-reliance on tools can induce input distribution shift, while overly conservative tool use limits effective exploration. To address this issue, we propose a unified framework TAO-RL that couples tool-aware trajectory filtering with entropy-guided exploration for efficient policy optimization. Specifically, at the data level, TAO-RL filters rollout trajectories along two criteria: discarding those where all tool invocations fail to execute, and removing those where all rollouts are either correct or incorrect, as both cases yield degenerate advantage estimates that contribute no discriminative learning signal. This joint filtering retains data that are both tool-capable and informative, establishing a high-quality training distribution. At the algorithmic level, we introduce a tool-aware entropy-guided bonus that reshapes the advantage function at post-tool-call tokens, encouraging the policy to explore more diverse reasoning paths at critical decision points. These two components are mutually reinforcing: trajectory filtering establishes a clean and informative training foundation, while entropy-guided exploration drives stronger reasoning behaviors at critical tool-interaction junctures. Extensive experiments on 7 7 challenging reasoning benchmarks across 3 3 model scales demonstrate the superiority of TAO-RL over existing methods.

Index Terms: Agentic reinforcement learning, tool-aware, trajectory filtering, reasoning, entropy I Introduction Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful post-training paradigm for improving the reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs) [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 ] . By enabling models to interact with external tools, such as code interpreters and search engines, LLMs have shown clear gains on complex multi-step reasoning tasks [ 8 , 9 , 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 ] . However, these gains come with a central challenge: once tools are integrated into the training loop, policy optimization often becomes substantially less stable [ 14 , 15 , 16 ] . Fig. 1: Comparison of tool-integrated reasoning (TIR) method and TAO-RL across Avg@16 in AIME 24&25, gradient norm and valid code rate under Qwen2.5-7B base model during training. This instability stems from how tool interaction reshapes model inputs. After each tool call, external execution results are injected back into the context, causing abrupt distributional shifts in token patterns and trajectory dynamics [ 17 , 14 , 18 ] . These shifts increase stochasticity and make policy updates brittle [ 19 , 12 ] . As illustrated in Fig. 1 , TIR exhibits large fluctuations in gradient norm, valid code rate, and average accuracy throughout training, empirically confirming that naively integrating tools destabilizes policy optimization. Furthermore, an overly conservative strategy that suppresses tool use is also undesirable, as it limits exploration and prevents the policy from discovering high-value agentic behaviors. Therefore, balancing training stability with effective exploration is a critical challenge in agentic RL. Existing works addressing this challenge focus primarily on the rollout process. One prominent line centers on rollout data curation, filtering trajectories with malformed formats or low-quality outputs [ 17 , 16 ] . But these approaches only discard trajectories based on format validity alone, ignoring whether the tool actually executed successfully and produced informative environmental feedback. Another line concentrates rollout resources on critical tokens through branching or targeted sampling [ 12 , 8 , 10 ] , these methods identify high-value decision points based on model-internal signals, without considering how successful tool outputs reshape the informational value of post-tool-call reasoning steps. As a result, neither line of work comprehensively accounts for the effects introduced by tool interaction. How to simultaneously stabilize training and enhance exploration for agentic policy optimization thus remains a critical challenge. To tackle this challenge, we propose TAO-RL , built on a key insight that stabilizing tool-integrated training noise followed by targeted exploration drives efficient optimization. TAO-RL couples tool-aware trajectory filtering with entropy-guided exploration, operating jointly at the data and algorithmic levels to drive effective policy optimization. At the data level , TAO-RL filters rollout trajectories according to two complementary criteria. First, trajectories in which tool invocations fail to execute are discarded, removing trajectories where tool interaction provides no informative environmental feedback and only injects noise into training. Second, trajectories where all rollouts are correct or all are incorrect are removed: the former indicates tasks already trivially solved by the current policy, yielding zero advantage estimates, while the latter provides no positive reward signal from which the policy can learn. This joint filtering retains trajectories that are both tool-capable and exhibit genuine answer diversity, constructing a high-quality training distribution that avoids the degenerate cases making uninformative or unstable policy updates. At the algorithmic level , we introduce a tool-aware entropy-guided exploration bonus based on the filtered training distribution. Rather than applying exploration incentives uniformly across all tokens, we identify tokens that follow tool executions and exhibit high entropy as critical decision points. By applying targeted entropy bonuses at these positions, TAO-RL encourages the policy to explore more diverse reasoning paths precisely where exploration is critical, progressively raising the reasoning ceiling without destabilizing the training foundation established by trajectory filtering. The two components are mutually reinforcing: trajectory filtering establishes a clean and informative training foundation by removing failed tool interactions and uninformative trajectories, while entropy-guided exploration drives stronger agentic reasoning behaviors at the critical tokens. Our contributions of this work can be summarized as follows: • We propose TAO-RL , a unified framework that innovatively couples data-level trajectory filtering with algorithm-level entropy-guided exploration, achieving stable training through principled data selection and effective exploration at critical tool-aware decision points. • TAO-RL integrates a two-criterion trajectory filtering strategy that jointly considers tool execution validity and answer discriminability to construct a high-quality training distribution, paired with an entropy-guided advantage reshaping mechanism that concentrates exploration incentives at post-tool-call tokens exhibiting high entropy. • Extensive experiments on seven challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks across three base model scales demonstrate that TAO-RL consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving superior reasoning performance and training stability across diverse tasks. The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section II provides an overview of related works, including agentic RL, and entropy-based exploration in RL. Section III details the necessary preliminaries. Section IV presents the proposed approach in detail. In section V , we introduce the experiments conducted to demonstrate the superiority of TAO-RL . Finally, section VI draws conclusions and discusses future works. II Related Work II-A Agentic RL Agentic RL extends LLMs from passive text generation to active environmental interaction, requiring multi-turn decision-making and precise tool-use strategies [ 20 , 21 , 14 , 22 , 23 , 24 ] . Recent advancements have transitioned from heuristic-based prompt engineering to end-to-end policy optimization via environmental feedback. On the architectural side, frameworks such as VERLTOOL [ 3 ] and ARTIST [ 2 ] focus on the co-design of distributed RL systems and agentic reasoning traces. Similarly, TORL [ 4 ] and ReTool [ 11 ] investigate the scalability of integrating code execution into the training loop to improve sample efficiency. On the algorithmic side, the focus shifts to stabilize the training of tool-integrated reasoning. For instance, SimpleTIR [ 17 ] mitigates gradient instability by filtering void turns, while GRPO-RoC [ 19 ] addresses environment noise through a resample-on-correct strategy. However, existing methods do not comprehensively account for the effects introduced by tool interaction. Data curation approaches filter trajectories based on format or output quality, but ignore whether tool executions actually succeeded or produced valid environmental feedback that is critical in agentic settings where failed tool calls inject pure noise into the training distribution. Token-level sampling identifies high-value decision points based on model-internal signals alone, without considering how successful tool outputs reshape the informational value of subsequent reasoning steps. Our work addresses both gaps within a unified framework: at the data level, we apply tool-aware trajectory filtering that jointly considers tool execution validity and answer discriminability; at the algorithmic level, we introduce an entropy-guided advantage reshaping mechanism that concentrates exploration incentives specifically at post-tool-call tokens. II-B Entropy-Based Exploration in RL Entropy-based exploration prevents entropy collapse, the rapid degradation of generation diversity frequently observed in DAPO [ 25 ] , standard PPO [ 26 ] and GRPO [ 27 ] . To counter this, methods like integrating entropy into advantage functions encourage exploratory reasoning [ 28 , 29 , 30 , 31 , 32 ] and selectively penalize high-covariance tokens to halt entropy decline [ 33 ] , and others restrict policy updates to pivotal high-entropy minority tokens based on the ”80/20 rule” [ 34 ] , or dynamically scale learning signals via entropy-based advantage reweighting [ 35 ] . In agentic RL, ARPO [ 10 ] leverages characteristic entropy spikes following tool invocations to balance rollout sampling, while AEPO [ 8 ] extends this by penalizing consecutive high-entropy steps to prevent over-branching. Despite these advances, existing entropy-based methods apply exploration incentives without accounting for the structural role of tool interaction.
